One unbroken centre line runs down the front and the back with no poles on it, and the mesh is exactly its own mirror image after finish. The trunk is a tube of one even count from the hip ring up to the ring under the armpits; it is closed above by a wide, shallow yoke grid laid over the shoulder girdle (trapezius, deltoid tops, upper chest and back), projected onto the sculpt, with a rectangular neck hole in its middle and an arm hole at each side, and the neck and arm tubes are bridged into those holes one-to-one, so the shoulder girdle carries about a dozen poles instead of a ring of a hundred Y-junctions. The hip ring is closed the same way with two leg holes either side of the centre column. Limbs are pole-free cylinders whose count is divisible by four; any count change that remains (under the jaw, at the ankle and wrist) is made with diamonds (one 3-pole and one 5-pole per step) gathered on the back or inside of the limb, mirrored across the plane, never a band of 3-to-1 merges across the front. Knees and elbows carry a three-ring band. Breasts, buttocks, shoulder blades, kneecaps and ears are all the same move: a rectangle of grid quads cut out by walking quad strips from a seed, its border inset as concentric rings that round off toward the feature's tip along the surface, a small grid in the middle, exactly four 5-poles at the rectangle's corners and four 3-poles at the centre grid, the grid outside undisturbed. Hands and feet end in aspect-correct grid caps: a flat grid across the toes, a 2x2 at every fingertip, a ringed heel, no spikes.

The head is built at 0.6 of the body's quad so the face has room, and the face is a nest, not a UV sphere: a mask rectangle from brow to cheekbone straddling the centre line, inset once (the goggle loop that crosses the centre line above the brows and dips at the bridge, enclosing both eyes) and gridded; two eye rectangles inside it inset three rings deep to a lid grid, with a ladder of rows between the inner corners; below the mask a nose-and-mouth rectangle inset twice (cheek loop, nasolabial loop) and gridded, holding a mouth rectangle with two rings and a lip grid and a nose rectangle with one ring domed to the nose tip. Hard surfaces are first-class in both paths. GOAL. HARD-1/3/5/13 on the alien and on any sculpt with armour, straps or buckles: a plate enclosed by a crease loop is its own patch: its outline is a mesh loop, the inside is a grid aligned to the plate's corners (rectangular plate) or concentric rings and a small grid (round boss, bore bottom), the count change to the body is absorbed in a gutter band on the body side, and no pole sits on the crease (HARD-10). Today the alien's chest plate, shoulder pads and hip plates are sliced by the body's distance rings into crumpled stair-steps (alien-built.png third panel): even with hard-features' ring snapping, plates whose outline is not a level set are still crossed.

INPUT. BodyFeatures.loops of class Plate (from hard-features): working-vertex loop, `inside` working faces (the smaller side), corners (Features.corners / loop_corners within 0.3 quad of the loop). The Work `w` handed to sweep_body (the mirrored ws when a plane is used) and a TriGrid nearest-point structure over its triangles (built once in sweep_body; rect-inset adds the pub(crate) TriGrid constructor). Output so far: out_p, quads (oriented).

STEPS, `fn plates(bf: &BodyFeatures, w, grid: &TriGrid, out_p, quads, plane, quad, debug) -> usize`, called after the first orient() (body.rs ~1171) and before bumps so the plate holes are cut in the plain body grid.
1. Skip loops with inside area < 4 quads^2 or > 40% of the mesh, and loops used as transverse rings.
2. Output quads under the plate: a quad is 'inside' if the nearest working triangle (TriGrid) of >= 3 of its corners is in `inside`, or its centroid's nearest triangle is inside. Make the set one disc: disc_border (rect.rs/body.rs 1423, pub(super)); if several border loops, drop the quads touching the extra loops and retry, up to 3 times; if still not a disc, or if the set touches a split strip / yoke hole row (any corner with valence 6 or any quad produced by a tour: keep a set of those quad indices from the build), skip the plate with a log line. Prefer a rectangular selection: if the loop has 4 corners and the inside quads form a regular strip region, use rect.rs grid_rect from the quad under the plate centre with a, b from the loop's extent so the hole border is a clean rectangle (4 corner poles) instead of a staircase.
3. Remove the quads (swap-remove; keep `quads` consistent), take the hole border B (nb points).
4. Outline ring: resample the loop's vertex positions along its arc at count n_r = even(perimeter/quad) with every corner forced to be a sample (split the arc between corners proportionally); start the ring at corner 0; orientation matched to B by the signed area against the mean normal.
5. Gutter: join B (nb) to the outline ring (n_r). If nb == n_r: plain quads, shift by min squared distance (join_band, layout.rs 2173). Else use reduce_band from the diamond task with the diamonds on the BODY side (the longer row is normally B: its extra points reduce toward the outline; place the diamonds midway between corners, never within 1 column of a corner); the merges thus sit between the body and the crease, never on it (HARD-10). Fallback join_band if the difference exceeds n_r/2 (log it).
6. Interior: with exactly 4 corners (or the 4 largest turning angles summing > 270 degrees), a = samples from corner 0 to 1, b = corner 1 to 2 (adjust one sample so a + b = n_r/2) and `cap_dims` extended to take the four corner indices as the grid corners (generalise cap_dims: `shift` = index of corner 0, a given); then rounds of inset are not needed: a flat Coons grid. Otherwise (round plate, 0 corners): inset_fill k = clamp(round(radius/quad) - 1, 1, 4), round 1.0, tip = Some(the inside region's most protruding point) then cap_dims. Project every interior point onto the working mesh restricted to the `inside` faces (a TriGrid over those triangles only, so a raised plate's interior does not snap to the body beside it).
7. Mirror: with a plane, when the reflected loop centroid matches another Plate loop's centroid within 1 quad, build the + one and mirror quad for quad (as bumps does at 1403-1417); plates straddling the plane are built whole (a even for the cap, pinned sample at the on-plane points); others are built per side.
8. orient() after each plate; log 'plate at ..: N quads cut, outline M (k corners), gutter d diamonds, grid a x b | k rings'; summary 'body: P plates built, S skipped'. Env ZR_NOPLATES=1.
9. Test shape: add `plated_tube()` to shape_tests (src/zremesh.rs): a cylinder with a raised rectangular plate (3 quads high) on its side and a round boss, built as a heightfield over a cylindrical grid so it is one closed mesh; register under ZR_ONLY=plated at 2 thousand quads with detect_edges on and ZR_BODYTOP so the builder runs on it.
